tier_reason: Upgraded from D. The peer-reviewed OOPSLA 2017 paper (opened from the project site's GitHub Pages repo) measures taco against Eigen sparse, Intel MKL, OSKI/pOSKI, uBLAS and Gmm++, plus SPLATT and the MATLAB Tensor Toolbox. It states GCC 5.4 and a two-socket Intel Xeon E5-2695 v2. The paper's artifact repo github.com/tensor-compiler/taco-bench (taco-bench.cpp with eigen-bench.h, mkl-bench.h, oski-bench.h, poski-bench.h, ublas-bench.h, gmm-bench.h) runs the SpMV, SDDMM, PLUS3, MATTRANSMUL and RESIDUAL comparisons, and its CMakeLists.txt gives the flags (-O3 -ffast-math -std=c++11). So code, compiler, flags and CPU are all public for the linear-algebra results; the tensor results against SPLATT and the Tensor Toolbox have no public harness there.

corrections.baseline: Eigen (sparse), Intel MKL, OSKI and pOSKI, uBLAS and Gmm++ for sparse linear algebra; SPLATT and the MATLAB Tensor Toolbox for sparse 3rd-order tensor kernels
corrections.workload: OOPSLA 2017 paper, Section 8. SpMV on six SuiteSparse matrices (rma10, cant, cop20k, scircuit, mac-econ, pwtk). Blocked SpMV against tuned OSKI/pOSKI. Compound kernels: SDDMM, PLUS3 (A = B + C + D), MATTRANSMUL (y = alpha A^T x + beta z) and RESIDUAL (y = b - Ax), the last two also on webbase-1M. 3rd-order tensor kernels TTV, TTM, MTTKRP, PLUS and INNERPROD on the Facebook, NELL-2 and NELL-1 tensors. Average cold-cache times, serial unless marked -par (12 threads on one socket).
corrections.claimed_speedup: The paper's headline is parity: performance 'competitive with best-in-class hand-optimized kernels in popular libraries' (abstract). SpMV (Fig. 14): 'competitive with Intel MKL and matches, if not slightly exceeds, single-threaded performance of all of the other libraries'; Eigen's bars sit at about 1.0x to 1.1x taco's time, and MKL is slightly faster on rma10 and cant. Compound operations (Fig. 16, bars read off the chart, so approximate): Eigen takes about 0.93x to 1.4x taco's time (largest on webbase-1M for MATTRANSMUL and RESIDUAL, where MKL and OSKI are also about 1.2x to 1.4x slower). Fig. 16 labels its off-scale bars: uBLAS 2,411.81x to 73,404.75x slower on SDDMM; PLUS3 bars at 4.88x to 5.79x (uBLAS) and 9.16x to 16.75x (Gmm++, 'about an order of magnitude slower'). Table 2 (serial unless noted): the MATLAB Tensor Toolbox is 9.329x to 1856x slower. MTTKRP against SPLATT: SPLATT takes 1.218x taco's time serial and 1.266x parallel on Facebook, but 0.7157x and 0.8371x on NELL-2 and NELL-1, and 0.6542x parallel on NELL-1, i.e. taco is up to 1.53x slower. Blocked SpMV: 'OSKI outperforms taco in almost all cases.'
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 5.4 (paper). taco-bench/CMakeLists.txt builds the harness and the header-only baselines with -O3 -ffast-math -std=c++11. taco JIT-compiles its generated C kernels with TACO_CFLAGS, which defaults to '-O3 -ffast-math -std=c99' in src/codegen/module.cpp at HEAD; the 2017 default was not checked. Baseline library versions (Eigen, MKL, OSKI, Boost uBLAS, Gmm++, SPLATT) are not stated.
corrections.hardware: Two-socket 12-core/24-thread 2.4 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2695 v2, 32 KB L1d, 30 MB L3 per socket, 128 GB RAM; parallel runs use 12 threads pinned to one socket with numactl
corrections.caveats: The README and paper claim parity, not a broad win. Against Eigen sparse, the incumbent, taco is roughly equal on SpMV and up to about 1.4x faster on fused compound operations; Eigen is slightly faster on some SDDMM and PLUS3 matrices. MKL is slightly faster on some SpMV matrices, tuned OSKI beats taco on blocked SpMV in almost all cases, and SPLATT's MTTKRP is up to 1.53x faster on NELL-1/NELL-2. The very large ratios have algorithmic causes: uBLAS SDDMM does Theta(n^3) dense work, and the Tensor Toolbox matricizes in MATLAB. The taco-bench harness covers only the linear-algebra libraries (no SPLATT or Tensor Toolbox code). Its last commits (2017-08-31 and 2017-09-01) disabled result validation for MKL SpMV, Gmm++ PLUS3 and uBLAS SDDMM/PLUS3. Baseline library versions are not stated. The measurements are from 2017 on an Ivy Bridge-EP Xeon with GCC 5.4 and -ffast-math on both sides; taco HEAD has changed since. Stale: last taco commit 2025-04-14, taco-bench last commit 2017-09-01.

notes: The paper and its artifact repo turned the D entry into A, though for a mostly-parity claim: real but modest wins over Eigen and MKL on fused kernels, large wins over uBLAS, Gmm++ and the Tensor Toolbox, and losses to tuned OSKI (blocked) and SPLATT (NELL tensors). tensor-compiler.org, arxiv.org, dspace.mit.edu, dl.acm.org and researchgate were blocked by egress. The PDF was read from the site's source repo (tensor-compiler/tensor-compiler.github.io, files/kjolstad-oopsla17-tensor-compiler.pdf); it is the published version (29 pp., CC-BY 4.0). The arXiv follow-ups 1802.10574 and 1804.10112 were not opened.
